name: CausalReorderBuffer
purpose: Buffer incoming events per (aggregate_id, sequence), drain in causal order, emit a single gap event when a predecessor times out.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class CausalReorderBuffer(Protocol):
    def offer(self, aggregate_id: str, sequence: int, event: Mapping[str, Any], deadline_ms: int) -> None: ...
    def next_ready(self, aggregate_id: str) -> Iterator[Mapping[str, Any]]: ...
    def timed_out(self, now_ms: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]: ...

invariants.rule: Events per aggregate_id drain in strictly monotonic sequence order.
An out-of-order event is held until its predecessor arrives OR its deadline_ms elapses.
On deadline expiry, timed_out() emits (aggregate_id, missing_sequence) exactly once.
After a gap is emitted, events at sequences > missing ARE drained (dropped predecessor cannot block forever).
Duplicate offer(agg, seq, ...) is idempotent; the second call is dropped silently.

extension_contract: Adopters MAY override _AggregateState to persist pending events for crash recovery; the five invariants MUST be preserved. Sequence type is monotonic int; a different type (e.g. Lamport tuples) is a different primitive.
consumption_example:
buf = InMemoryCausalReorderBuffer()
buf.offer('acct-42', 1, {'kind': 'credit'}, deadline_ms=5000)
buf.offer('acct-42', 0, {'kind': 'opened'}, deadline_ms=5000)
for ev in buf.next_ready('acct-42'):
    apply(ev)
for agg, missing in buf.timed_out(now_ms=9999):
    alert(agg, missing)
why_essential: Without a per-aggregate reorder buffer, every consumer reinvents out-of-order handling and diverges on gap semantics; a single dropped message either stalls the aggregate forever or corrupts state silently.
alternatives_considered: Strict blocking on head — a dropped predecessor stalls the aggregate forever; unacceptable for availability.
Silently drop out-of-order events — loses recent state and is invisible to SRE.
Client-side sort per consumer — duplicates logic and diverges on deadline semantics.
